subject: Problem for specifying a model with matrices

messages.author: f97b0bfe799a761a
messages.subject: Problem for specifying a model with matrices
parts:
Dear INLA forum, 

We would like to implement a model such as

y = M %*% beta + G %*% b

where M and G are matrices, beta fixed regression coefficients and b individuals effects which are random.

The problem is that beta is a vector of fixed effects and b has to be a vector which includes random effects. We have written the following code but in this we would be introducing all the effects as if they were random. How can we fix it?

M <- cbind(X,G%*%Z)
y = M %*% beta + G %*% b 
weight.beta <- c(1,25)
Qz <- diag(1,dim(G)[2])
nb <- dim(M)[2]
nz <- dim(G)[2]

idx.beta = c(1:nb, rep(NA, nz))
idx.b = c(rep(NA, nb), 1:nz)
hyper.fixed = list(prec = list(initial = log(0.001), fixed=TRUE))
formula = Y ~ -1 + f(idx.beta,  model="iid", hyper = hyper.fixed, constr = FALSE)+ f(idx.b, model="generic", Cmatrix=Qz)
result = inla(formula, family = "binomial", data = list(y=Y, idx.beta=idx.beta, idx.b=idx.b), control.predictor = list(A=cBind(M, G)))

Thank you very much, 

Laura
